history: The GD-chassis WRX STI was a landmark moment for Subaru in North America — the first generation of the STI officially sold in the United States. Launched for the 2004 model year, the GD STI brought the legendary rally-bred performance that Japanese and European enthusiasts had enjoyed for years to American shores for the first time.

Built on the GD platform shared with the standard WRX, the STI received a host of upgrades that set it apart: the larger EJ257 2.5-liter turbocharged flat-four, Brembo brakes, Bilstein dampers, a close-ratio 6-speed manual, and Subaru's Driver Controlled Center Differential (DCCD) system that allowed real-time adjustment of the AWD torque split.

The GD STI quickly earned a reputation as one of the finest driver's cars of its era. Its combination of raw turbocharged punch, brilliant AWD traction, and communicative chassis made it a favorite on both the street and in competition. The 2005 and 2006 models refined the package further, and the 2006 STI is widely considered the sweet spot of the generation.

The GD generation concluded with the 2007 model year, making way for the GR hatchback. Today the GD STI is highly sought after by collectors and enthusiasts — particularly low-mileage examples and the rare Special Edition models produced during this era.
did_you_know: The GD STI's gold BBS wheels became one of the most iconic wheel designs in performance car history. The 17-inch gold-painted BBS forged alloys were standard equipment and remain a defining visual signature of the generation — so much so that aftermarket replicas are still widely sold today.

trims.name: WRX STI
trims.description: The sole trim for North America, arriving fully loaded with Brembo brakes, Bilstein dampers, gold BBS wheels, DCCD AWD, and the 300hp EJ257 engine.

trims.name: STI Limited
trims.description: Added leather seating, a sunroof, and additional interior comfort features to the standard STI performance package.

trims.name: STI Special Edition
trims.description: Limited run of 1,000 units in WR Blue with additional interior trim and a numbered plaque. One of the most collectible GD examples today.

variants.name: 2005 Special Edition
variants.description: A 1,000-unit limited run celebrating the STI's US debut. Exclusively in WR Blue Pearl with a numbered dash plaque and special floor mats — already a sought-after collector's piece.

variants.name: JDM Spec C
variants.description: The Japan-market Spec C variant of the GD STI featured significant weight reduction through lighter glass, thinner sound deadening, and a revised intake. Never officially sold in the US but widely imported.
